newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent posts fresh gains, NYMEX stronger.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent posts fresh gains, NYMEX stronger.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures posted fresh gains on Thursday, helped by a spurt of local buying and a strong NYMEX opening, brokers.
New front month September was trading at $18.49 a barrel at 1406 GMT, up 19 cents on the day and one cent off the high.
Gas oil futures were also stronger. August was up $1.75 a tonne at $165.50.
"Locals have been trying to take it higher since early afternoon," said one IPE broker.
The buying pushed September Brent out of its morning range of $18.26 to $18.34 and a healthy NYMEX WTI opening pushed the London contract above resistance at $18.45.
August WTI started 15 cents higher at $19.80, at the top end of expectations, and quickly pushed further into positive territory to trade at $19.90.
IPE dealers said there were few fresh headlines to give fundamental direction.
Players in the market continued to wait for fresh signs of possible renewed Iraqi exports.

The U.N. confirmed late on Wednesday that Iraq will not be allowed to carry more than five percent of its $1 billion allowance over into the second 90-day tranche of a current six-month, $2 billion oil-for-food sales deal, which came into effect on June 8.

Because of delays in lifting Iraqi crude so far this means the $1 billion worth of oil will have to be squeezed into a much shorter time period, which could mean exports of over 1.5 million barrels per day in August or early September.
In Nigeria, Shell said it had reopened 12 flow stations which were shut after a fire last week, which took out about 135,000 barrels of lost production.
